correctness.rationale: Exact binomial ratio gives fixed-n boundary. For r>=2 the falling-factorial geometric mean has negative second derivative by strict variance inequality, so the objective has at most one continuous trough. Its left tangent intercept and asymptotic tangent intercept locate the only regimes. The factorial threshold at r=11 follows from ten exact signs plus a strict induction. The isolated finite neighbor comparisons are certified using 40-digit integer nth-root enclosures in the attached standard-library checker. All quantifiers and nonattainment cases have been checked; finite checks do not prove global concavity, which is proven analytically.

originality.rationale: The motivating article derives each fixed-count crossing but does not minimize those crossings over homogeneous trial counts for all r. Its unrestricted r>=3 result exploits deterministic support shifts, unavailable when all trials share an interior p. Strict concavity and exact factorial signs show a distinct finite-to-Poisson optimizer transition at r=11. value.rationale: The question is the homogeneous-trial inverse design counterpart of a recently developed nonadjacent atom-reversal problem. The complete classification answers whether a few concentrated Bernoulli trials, an intermediate finite trial count, or a diffuse Poisson limit minimizes the required mean. It exhibits nontrivial intermediate integers including 294 and a sharp change to unattained Poissonization at r=11, beyond simply recomputing a familiar binomial probability.
